_comment: The cockpit's own map, for the assistant: every view and control, where it is and what it does. Keep it in step with the page: the cockpit tests check that every view here is in the page's route table (core.js PAGE_ROUTES) with the same route, and that every control appears as data-control.

views.label: Home
views.purpose: the dashboard for your lens: key figures, decisions waiting, the delivery square, health and more, in your own layout

views.label: Delivery square
views.purpose: needs arriving from the operation, concepts to validate, the factory, end-user feedback and what runs in production

views.label: Capability catalogue
views.purpose: every capability: in use, pilot or proposed, what it does, and whether its capability pack is valid

views.label: Projects
views.purpose: every project with its state, now line and health

views.label: All decisions
views.purpose: every card you may decide across projects, including updates and concepts, by kind, project or age

views.label: Floor
views.purpose: the factory across all projects: gate pass rate, pipeline, models, spend

views.label: Settings
views.purpose: the modules in use, embeds for websites, appearance, and sign-in links for another tab

views.label: Shape it in chat
views.purpose: work out a need with Rihma in conversation: start from nothing, a sentence or a file, see a draft brief take shape beside the chat and edit it, then create the project from it

views.label: Models setup
views.purpose: which model answers for each role: its endpoint, model name and API key, local or hosted, with a Test that sends a tiny prompt

views.label: Runners (cell runners)
views.purpose: which harness runs the factory's cells: Gnomon, which enforces the rules during a run, or another harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or a command you name) that IT approves on a card with its version pinned and that is checked after every run; per project and per role

views.label: Overview
views.purpose: a project's health, forecast, now line and what waits on you

views.label: Inbox
views.purpose: the cards you may decide, with the verdicts you may give

views.label: Questions
views.purpose: the panel's questions with options; answer or let Rihma assume

views.label: Assumptions
views.purpose: what Rihma assumed, with due dates; confirm or refute

views.label: Plan
views.purpose: the plan waiting for approval; edit a requirement, approve or reject with a reason

views.label: Spec & contract
views.purpose: requirements and criteria with sources and evidence chips

views.label: Tasks
views.purpose: the task board, timeline or table, and the live view of the running cell

views.label: Cell
views.purpose: every Gnomon run: role, model, verdict, chain, tokens, cost

views.label: Releases
views.purpose: deliveries with their capability pack: environments, holdouts, shadow, canary

views.label: Try it
views.purpose: the checklist against the running release, and reporting what you saw

views.label: Changes
views.purpose: report a change or feedback; see triage and impact

views.label: Ledger
views.purpose: every recorded event, who acted, and whether the chain is intact

views.label: Evidence
views.purpose: the attestation, the control table and the evidence pack export, for compliance

views.label: Jobs
views.purpose: background runs started from the cockpit

views.label: Track
views.purpose: whether a project stays on track against its approved plan, every figure with its basis, the human checkpoints a person looks at, the autopilot in a sandbox and the delegations

views.label: Outputs
views.purpose: what each audience receives: choose the outputs, then build and download them from the project's records and its release (a web app with sign-in, a container, an API description, a delivery report, an evidence pack, the source). A choice made with the new-project request is told to intake, never asked again, and kept in the brief; with sign-in, a factory check the sign-in turns away says not measured (docs/guides/outputs.md)

views.label: Assessment
views.purpose: an adopted system judged from five perspectives (CI/CD governance, maintenance, security, compliance, architecture and operations), each finding with its evidence, severity and a suggested change; versions compared; findings filed as changes

views.label: Automations
views.purpose: every automation across the factory, with scope filters: a trigger (a schedule, a recorded event, an inbound webhook ringing, new commits on a branch), an optional guard, an action and a scope, run with its owner's rights; templates, pause and resume, run now, a dry run and the history of runs. An automation never decides a card (docs/guides/automations.md)

views.label: Automations (project)
views.purpose: the automations that reach one project, its tags, and what ran on it, with a builder whose scope starts at this project

views.label: Console
views.purpose: commands in the project's workspace (its attached repository, your workspace or the console's working copy): the project's own commands as buttons (stated test, build and lint commands, package.json scripts, Makefile targets, CI steps) or a typed one, Gnomon asked to do something under its own governance, the output line by line with a time limit and Stop, and Open a terminal here for full-screen programs; every one recorded in the ledger, for developers and IT (docs/guides/console-and-checks.md)

views.label: Health (project)
views.purpose: the project's checks for maintenance and administration: the test suite, CI/CD status, dependency audit, secret scan, licences, SBOM, an HTTP probe, the repo gate, the security gate and custom commands, each passed, failed or not measured with its evidence, its trend and when it last ran; Run now and enable a check with a schedule

views.label: Health
views.purpose: every project's checks across the factory: what passes, what fails and what is not measured, the failing list, and a check enabled on several projects at once

views.label: Alignment
views.purpose: an adopted or attached project aligned with its repository's own structure: the requirements, acceptance criteria (given/when/then, EARS, Gherkin), tests, tasks, ADRs and API contracts the team keeps there (spec-kit, Kiro, BMAD, agent-os, PRDs, user stories), each proposed for the project's contract and accepted, edited or rejected; which tests trace to which criteria and how sure; the gaps (requirements with no test, tests with no requirement, criteria not testable as written, specs older than the code, CI that does not run the tests); suggested changes for the repository as text or a patch, never written there; and the drift after the repository changed. The same: `rihmasto align <pid>`

views.label: Insights
views.purpose: health, compliance, governance, security, context drift, QA and token, skill and memory usage across the factory or for one project, over 24 hours, 7 or 30 days or all records: stat tiles and charts counted from the records, each with a one-line insight, what is not measured and how to measure it, and an export to your own observability tools

views.label: Project insights
views.purpose: one project's insights: health, compliance, governance, security, context drift, QA and usage of its agentic work, from its own records

views.label: Knowledge graph
views.purpose: every project's records as a knowledge graph, as the ontology links them: requirements, criteria, tests, tasks, questions, assumptions, decisions, changes, releases and agent runs, with filters by kind, relation, state, time and words, focus on a node, the issues found (requirements no test checks, tests without a requirement, decisions overturned) and a table of nodes and relations

views.label: Project knowledge graph
views.purpose: one project's records as a knowledge graph: what each requirement rests on and what checks it, with filters, focus on a node, its details and a link to its record, issues highlighted, and a table mode; save your filters as a view, pin a slice to Home

views.label: Review
views.purpose: since you last looked: what agents and automations did across your projects, grouped by what needs you (waiting on you, went wrong, decided for you, shipped, from your IDE, cost and usage), each with its record and who or what did it; approve, decline, overturn, report a change or mark reviewed in place
synonyms: what happened while i was away

views.label: Review
views.purpose: since you last looked, for one project: what its agents shipped, what went wrong, what was decided in your name and what waits on you
synonyms: since i last looked at this project

views.label: Agent channel
views.purpose: one threaded conversation per project between people, Rihma's agents (analyst, verifier) and the coding agents working on it from a terminal or an IDE (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor): their progress, questions and Rihma's answers, proposed answers a person confirms or rejects, hand-offs, gate and check results, each with a trace of what it rests on; pause the channel, filter by agent or kind, and post with @analyst or @verifier (docs/guides/agentic-help.md)

views.label: Agent activity
views.purpose: every project's agent channel across the factory: who is talking, the last message, and any agent proposal waiting on a person

views.label: AI tools
views.purpose: the Agents capsule's view of an adopted or attached project's AI coding tools (instructions, skills, subagents, commands, hooks, MCP servers) and the MCP configuration to work on it from your IDE

views.label: Context
views.purpose: what Rihmasto knows about this project and where it came from (the request, the material, the repository, the conventions, the canon, the ledger, the graph, the spec and contract, model usage, what is stale, what is kept on disk), and what each Rihma agent is given right now: every context pack with its parts, sizes, budget and what was compressed or left out

views.label: Data and context
views.purpose: the factory's data and context health: every store of the factory home with its size, every ledger's integrity, retention and a signed clean-up, and per agent role the context pack sizes, over-budget packs and the cache-friendly prefix

views.label: Destinations
views.purpose: every place the capability goes: where it runs (each environment on its paved road, the release and its URL), the data systems and integrations it reaches, the channels it is used through (website chats, Teams, Slack, email, its MCP and API faces) and where it is published (container and MCP registries, outputs); each with its state and health, and deliver to test, promote to production, publish, open and investigate (docs/guides/destinations.md)

views.label: Agent sessions
views.purpose: for developers and IT, when Agent observability is on for the project: what the IDE agents (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode) did in its repository, read from your own agent observability hub: sessions by harness over time, rework hotspots, failures and whether they were recovered, sessions that read the contract before editing, session trajectories and the hub's hash-chain check, each with a link into the hub; not measured, with how to instrument the repository, when the hub has nothing (docs/guides/agent-observability.md)

views.label: Incidents
views.purpose: every incident across the factory (a server error, a failed job, a broken or empty view, a refused step, a failed check or automation, a report): what happened in plain words, its context, the remedies Rihmasto offers (learned ones first), Investigate with Rihma, a fix sent as a pull request, and What Rihmasto learned with counts and who approved each remedy; the feedback proposals to approve (docs/guides/self-healing.md)

views.label: Incidents
views.purpose: this project's incidents: what happened, its fingerprint and context, the remedies offered, the investigation by a Rihma agent with its trace, a fix through the gate and its pull request, and what Rihmasto learned here

controls.label: Scope switcher
controls.where: the scope bar at the top of every page: All projects, or Project: <title>
controls.does: says whether you look at one project or all of them, and switches project (recent first) or goes back to all projects; inside a project the frame takes the project's colour

controls.label: Capsules
controls.where: a project's page, below its header: Now, Build, Run, Govern and Agents
controls.does: group the project's views by purpose; each opens its own short row of tabs, and a count says what waits on you there. Now: Overview, Inbox, Review; Build: Spec & contract, Tasks, Changes, Alignment, Console; Run: Releases, Outputs, Health, Automations; Govern: Evidence, Track, Insights, Ledger; Agents: Channel, AI tools

controls.label: Customize this view
controls.where: Customize in the top bar, on any page but Home
controls.does: shows, hides, moves and resizes the sections of the view you are on, kept for you, with Reset; a section holding a decision that waits on you is never hidden

controls.label: Hide or pin a tab
controls.where: Customize on a project page, on each tab of the capsule row
controls.does: hides a tab you never use or pins a favourite to the top row, kept for you

controls.label: Square scope
controls.where: the Delivery square, at the top
controls.does: shows the square for all projects or for one project; each lane's count opens its items

controls.label: What Rihma talks about
controls.where: the top of the Ask Rihma panel
controls.does: says whether Rihma answers about this view, this project or the whole platform, and switches it; each scope keeps its own conversation

controls.label: Persona switcher
controls.where: the person chip, top right
controls.does: changes whose view you see and what you may decide

controls.label: Lens switcher
controls.where: top bar
controls.does: shows the same work for a purpose: business, concept, delivery, operations, compliance or insight

controls.label: Pause
controls.where: project header
controls.does: asks the project to stop at the next safe point

controls.label: Resume
controls.where: project header, when paused
controls.does: lets a paused project continue

controls.label: Answer
controls.where: a question card
controls.does: records your answer as the owner's word

controls.label: Let Rihma assume
controls.where: a question card
controls.does: takes the panel's proposal as an assumption with a due date

controls.label: Verdict buttons
controls.where: an Inbox card, under its Decide line (Your choice), or the decisions widget
controls.does: decides the card with your name and persona: pick one of its choices (each says what it means), optionally say why, then Confirm; nothing is chosen for you

controls.label: Report a change
controls.where: Changes view and Try it
controls.does: files feedback or a change; it is triaged and routed back

controls.label: Comment
controls.where: requirements, tasks and releases; on an Inbox card, Add a comment at its foot, separate from the decision
controls.does: adds a remark without deciding anything; it can be promoted into a change

controls.label: Jump to (Ctrl+K)
controls.where: top bar
controls.does: jumps to any page, project, view or open card

controls.label: Assistant
controls.where: bottom right, or press /
controls.does: answers questions about the cockpit and your projects, and proposes actions you confirm

controls.label: Customize
controls.where: top bar, on every page
controls.does: on Home rearranges, resizes, adds or removes the dashboard's widgets (Done saves your own layout); on any other page shows, hides, moves and resizes that view's sections, and in a project hides or pins its tabs

controls.label: Theme
controls.where: top bar
controls.does: switches dark, light or system, the accent colour and the corners

controls.label: Density
controls.where: top bar
controls.does: switches between comfortable and compact spacing

controls.label: Adopt an existing project
controls.where: New project, Start from: An existing project
controls.does: adopts an existing project from a folder on this machine or a git address: a folder is scanned first, one that is not a git repository is snapshotted into a baseline repository (your folder is never changed), and one with no code is offered as material for a new project instead; Rihmasto records its tests as a baseline and then monitors, maintains or improves it

controls.label: Scan the folder
controls.where: New project, after you give a folder (in An existing project, or a folder path as the need)
controls.does: shows what Rihmasto would read of the folder before anything is sent or created: each file read in full, summarised, only listed or skipped, with the reason (code becomes an inventory, secret-looking files are never opened, the budget reads the most telling files first and says what it cut) and the characters it comes to and where they would go; untick a file to leave it out, then create or adopt the project. The same map: `rihmasto scan <folder>`

controls.label: Confidential: keep on local models
controls.where: New project, both paths
controls.does: records the project as confidential: intake and every model call for it may go only to a model on this machine or a private network address; a role routed to a hosted model is refused with the role named and how to set up a local model (docs/guides/local-models.md), never sent. The setting is in the ledger
synonyms: do not send to the cloud

controls.label: New project
controls.where: sidebar and Projects
controls.does: starts a project from a need: its work profile and how it runs (a posture with its weights, or a maturity and mode)

controls.label: Log a signal
controls.where: the delivery square
controls.does: records a need that arrived from the operation, to be triaged

controls.label: Validate a concept
controls.where: the delivery square
controls.does: turns a concept into a project, after you edit its title, profile, maturity and mode

controls.label: Export evidence pack
controls.where: a project's Evidence tab and the Compliance lens
controls.does: exports a zip with the attestation, decisions, gate verdicts and the whole record, downloaded once

controls.label: Build the capability pack
controls.where: a project's Releases tab
controls.does: builds the latest release's capability pack, signed with your name; a new version only when what it names changed. Showing the pack never builds it

controls.label: Create an embed
controls.where: Settings
controls.does: makes a chat window for a website that files feedback or needs; its key is shown once

controls.label: Autonomy cap
controls.where: the Compliance lens and the project header
controls.does: sets how far the factory may act alone, with a reason

controls.label: Intake summary
controls.where: a project's Questions view
controls.does: shows side by side what your input stated, with its document and lines, what was put to a person and what was assumed, and which questions were not asked because they only restate your input (a question about anything more is asked, and a blocking one always reaches a person, quoting the lines it rests on)

controls.label: Track pill
controls.where: the project header
controls.does: the project's one on-track answer (it carries every reason the health reads): whether the project is on track against its approved plan, not measured before a plan is approved, with a checkpoint due or an autopilot running, and opens the Track view

controls.label: Set checkpoints and a budget
controls.where: a project's Track view
controls.does: a plan owner picks the stage boundaries a person must look at, whether a due one holds the run, a due date and a cost budget

controls.label: I looked
controls.where: a due checkpoint in a project's Track view
controls.does: records, signed, that you looked at the stage; a run the checkpoint held goes on at its next pass

controls.label: Start the autopilot
controls.where: a project's Track view
controls.does: delegates the card kinds you choose to the factory's rules until a time and runs the project on its own, bound to a sandbox

controls.label: Stop the autopilot
controls.where: a project's Track view, while an autopilot holds it
controls.does: stops the run at once: its delegation is revoked and what it held back in the sandbox is released; a pass still under way delivers nothing more and ends at its next safe point, and then you run the project yourself to deliver

controls.label: Revoke a delegation
controls.where: a delegation in a project's Track view
controls.does: stops a delegation at once: its next card waits for a person

controls.label: Choose the outputs
controls.where: a project's Outputs tab
controls.does: records which outputs the project delivers, with your name and why; choosing the web app with sign-in adds the paved road's sign-in to the product

controls.label: Build and download an output
controls.where: a project's Outputs tab, on each output's card
controls.does: builds one chosen output from the records and the release, signed with your name, and downloads it once

controls.label: Build every chosen output
controls.where: a project's Outputs tab
controls.does: builds every chosen output at once; each card then offers its file as a one-time download

controls.label: Download a built output
controls.where: an output's card, after a build
controls.does: downloads the file a build just made; the link works once

controls.label: Modules
controls.where: Settings, and the first-run choice on a new factory
controls.does: chooses which parts of Rihmasto this factory or one project uses: a preset such as spec only or gate my code, or each module; a module that is off says what it would add, and the change is signed and recorded

controls.label: Revoke an embed
controls.where: Settings, Embeds
controls.does: stops a website's chat for good, signed with your name; a product owner, business owner or IT may, and it stays open while Integrations is off

controls.label: Project settings
controls.where: a project's header
controls.does: changes what was set when the project was made: its title, kind of work (template), mode and maturity, with a preview of what the change means for the questions, spec and plan already done; signed with a reason, and nothing is deleted

controls.label: Go back a step
controls.where: Project settings, and a project's What's next strip
controls.does: sends a project back to its material, questions, spec or plan so that step runs again; what it sets aside is kept as superseded, and a released project changes through the change loop instead

controls.label: Add material
controls.where: Project settings, and a project's What's next strip
controls.does: adds more of the request to a project later (text, or a file or folder path) and lets the panel ask only about what is new; the original request and every answer are kept

controls.label: What's next
controls.where: a project's Overview
controls.does: says what the project waits for, who can act, and the buttons that move it forward: a card to decide, a question to answer, a retry, material to add or a setting to change

controls.label: Look at the spec before building: Go or Skip
controls.where: a project's What's next strip, and its Inbox card
controls.does: at explore and demo maturity the factory waits once, before the first build, for a person's go-ahead on the spec: Go builds it, Skip builds it without the look; either is signed and the run goes on
synonyms: why does it wait before building

controls.label: Build without waiting for me
controls.where: Project settings, and New project
controls.does: turns off the go-ahead on the spec for this project: at explore and demo it builds the spec as written, without waiting for a person's Go or Skip

controls.label: Shape it in chat
controls.where: Home's header, and New project
controls.does: opens a conversation with Rihma to work out what is needed

controls.label: Start the conversation
controls.where: Shape it in chat
controls.does: opens a new conversation, with a first message and a file or folder if you give them

controls.label: Send to Rihma
controls.where: Shape it in chat, a conversation
controls.does: sends your message; Rihma answers with one or two questions and updates the draft

controls.label: Attach a file or folder
controls.where: Shape it in chat, a conversation
controls.does: adds text, Markdown or a Word document, or a folder on the cockpit's machine, for Rihma to read

controls.label: Save the draft
controls.where: Shape it in chat, beside the conversation
controls.does: keeps your own words in the draft brief; Rihma leaves the fields you edited as you wrote them

controls.label: Create the project from this
controls.where: Shape it in chat, under the draft
controls.does: creates the project from the draft, with the work profile, mode and maturity you choose and Rihma's suggestion
synonyms: turn the chat into a project

controls.label: Open Models setup
controls.where: Settings, and Home while no model answers
controls.does: opens the page where each role's model and endpoint is set and tested

controls.label: Change a role's model
controls.where: Models setup, a role
controls.does: points a role at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and model, with its key as a variable's name or stored outside the repository

controls.label: Test a model
controls.where: Models setup, a role
controls.does: sends the role's endpoint a tiny prompt and says how fast it answered, or the error

controls.label: Back to the shipped model
controls.where: Models setup, a role set on this machine
controls.does: takes the role back to the shipped routing

controls.label: On my own network
controls.where: Models setup, the change form
controls.does: declares a model server reached by name on your own network (this machine, a tailnet or a VPN) as local, so a confidential project may use it; addresses like 127.0.0.1, 192.168.x.x and 100.x.x.x count already

controls.label: Model presets
controls.where: Models setup, the change form
controls.does: fills the form for llama.cpp, Ollama or vLLM on this machine, OpenCode Go, or a hosted OpenAI-compatible provider

controls.label: Use Claude Code
controls.where: Models setup, Use the coding agent you already have; Home's Set up a model card when Claude Code is found
controls.does: answers every text role (the analyst, the holdout author, the verifier and the assistant), or the roles chosen, with the Claude Code on this machine and your own login, run headless with no tools; no API key needed. Slower than an API endpoint, and it spends your own subscription. Each call is recorded as run by Claude Code, not through Gnomon's lane

controls.label: Use Codex
controls.where: Models setup, Use the coding agent you already have
controls.does: answers the chosen text roles with the Codex on this machine, run headless in its read-only sandbox; no API key needed in Rihmasto. Slower than an API endpoint, and it spends your own plan

controls.label: Use OpenCode
controls.where: Models setup, Use the coding agent you already have
controls.does: answers the chosen text roles with the OpenCode on this machine, run headless with every tool off; name its model (provider/model) or family. Declared private when it runs a model on your own network

controls.label: Posture
controls.where: the project header and Project settings (the Posture chip), and How it runs in the New project dialog (a need or an existing project)
controls.does: chooses how a project runs (prototype, balanced, production or regulated) with priority weights for ux, security, compliance, speed and cost; shows what it will do before you choose, and what a change does now and later; lists what holds the project now (a go-ahead card and who decides it, an assumption to confirm, an evidence pack due before staging or production)

controls.label: Assess now
controls.where: an adopted project's Assessment tab
controls.does: reads the repository's main by rule from five perspectives and records a new assessment version signed with your name; with 'Ask the panel too' the panel's model proposes more, kept apart as opinions

controls.label: Correct or add to it
controls.where: an adopted project's Overview, in What Rihmasto understood
controls.does: opens Add material to correct or add to what Rihmasto understood about the project: a description, documents, notes

controls.label: Accept, defer or reject selected
controls.where: a project's Inbox, above the change cards
controls.does: decides several change cards together with one reason; each is signed and recorded on its own, and accepted ones go into the spec and the contract

controls.label: Go on with the suggested defaults
controls.where: a project's Inbox, above the questions
controls.does: goes on with each open question's suggested default, recorded as your choice and open to a real answer later

controls.label: Ask Rihma what went wrong
controls.where: Jobs, on a failed job
controls.does: asks Rihma why the job failed; it answers by rule from the job's own log, with what to do next

controls.label: Ask Rihma what to fix first
controls.where: an adopted project's Assessment tab, in Fix what matters
controls.does: asks Rihma which open findings to fix first and why; it answers by rule from the latest assessment, and the same block selects the top findings, critical and high, or all open ones

controls.label: Assessment progress
controls.where: an adopted project's Assessment tab while an assessment runs, small on its Overview
controls.does: shows the assessment live, area by area: reading the code, one rule check per area and the security scan, each perspective of the panel with the model that answers, the record; each tile fills as its step runs and ends, with its findings as they land, the time it has taken and an estimate from the earlier runs (the first run has none); press a tile for that area's findings so far; when it ends it opens the result. The same in Ask Rihma: how is the assessment going?

controls.label: Cancel the assessment
controls.where: the assessment's progress, while it runs
controls.does: stops the running assessment after the step that runs now, signed with your name; nothing it did so far is recorded

controls.label: Assessing (Overview)
controls.where: a project's Overview while its assessment runs
controls.does: the assessment's progress, small, with the way to its Assessment tab; when it ends it says how

controls.label: Scan progress
controls.where: Add a project or Feed in a folder, while the folder is scanned
controls.does: shows the folder scan's steps live: looking through the folder, opening what matters, the material map; Cancel the scan stops it

controls.label: File as changes
controls.where: an adopted project's Assessment tab, below the findings
controls.does: turns the findings you tick into change cards from the assessment, each as its own suggested or chosen kind

controls.label: AI tools in this project
controls.where: an adopted or attached project's Overview
controls.does: shows how the team's AI coding tools are set up in the repository, each with where it is: project instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules, Cursor rules with their globs, Copilot, Windsurf and Cline rules), Claude skills with their bundled files, subagents, slash commands, hooks and permission rules, and MCP servers by name; and the build and test commands the instructions state. Nothing found is run; personal settings are listed, never read. Skills and MCP servers are candidates for Rihmasto's catalogue only, after a person approves. The same list: `rihmasto ide <pid>`

controls.label: Work on it from your IDE
controls.where: an adopted or attached project's Overview, beside AI tools in this project
controls.does: gives ready-to-paste MCP configuration for Claude Code (.mcp.json or claude mcp add), Cursor (.cursor/mcp.json) and Codex pointing at Rihmasto's own MCP server, signed with your name and persona, and says how a developer's change comes back: a workspace's submission through the gate on an adopted project, `rihmasto repo gate` on an attached one. The IDE is the inner loop, Rihmasto the outer loop. The same: `rihmasto ide <pid>`

controls.label: Copy the section
controls.where: Work on it from your IDE, on an adopted or attached project's Overview
controls.does: copies or downloads the text "Rihmasto's contract and open questions for your IDE agent" (the contract, what waits on a decision, how a change comes back, the rules) for you to paste into your project's AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md yourself; Rihmasto never writes into your folder. The same: `rihmasto ide <pid> --section`

controls.label: Read the repository
controls.where: an adopted or attached project's Alignment tab, at the top
controls.does: reads the repository's committed revision by rule and proposes how its own specs, criteria, tests, tasks, decisions and API contracts map onto the project, with the gaps between them; signed with your name, runs nothing it finds and writes nothing to the repository; again after the repository changed, it shows what is new, changed or removed. The same: `rihmasto align <pid> --scan`

controls.label: Accept, Edit or Reject an alignment item
controls.where: each item of an adopted or attached project's Alignment tab
controls.does: accepts a proposed requirement, criterion, test trace, task, decision, API contract reference or gap into the project (Edit changes it first), or rejects it; accepting a requirement or criterion writes it into the project's contract, customer-endorsed by you and noted as imported from the repository, and the ledger records alignment_accepted with the item ids. The same: `rihmasto align <pid> accept|edit|reject <item>`
synonyms: accept a requirement from my repo

controls.label: Accept all open
controls.where: each group's header in an adopted or attached project's Alignment tab
controls.does: accepts every open item of one group (requirements, criteria, tests trace, tasks, decisions, API contracts or gaps) at once, signed with your name

controls.label: Copy or download a suggested change
controls.where: Suggested changes for your repository, in an adopted or attached project's Alignment tab
controls.does: copies a suggested change for your repository (criterion ids in test names, a task list entry, a CI job that runs the tests, tests to write, criteria to restate) or downloads it as a patch to apply with git apply; Rihmasto never writes into your repository

controls.label: Runtime and faces
controls.where: a project's Releases tab, in its capability pack
controls.does: shows what a small capability needs where it runs (what starts it, its tools, model roles, integrations and secrets by name) and how to reach each of its faces: MCP, the OpenAI-compatible chat, the website embed and HTTP, with the command that serves it

controls.label: Access note
controls.where: the top bar, beside the person chip; on a narrow screen, the person menu
controls.does: says who signs decisions: with a single operator, personas are self-declared; with access enforced, the person the organisation's sign-in verified, the personas IT granted, when the session ends with the sign-in token, and where untrusted code runs (the isolation runner: the gate's tests, adoption's baseline, local products and Gnomon cells; the kernel scrubs a lane's .git before its own git runs there, refuses a cell's work that holds a nested repository, ignores replace refs and grafts, and copies the head's tests to the gate's base from git, never following a link). A name from the token that looks like a listed person's name (lookalike letters and invisible characters included) carries the subject after it; the key file takes public keys only
synonyms: cell refused for a nested repository
what the kernel does with a lane's .git
private key in the key file

controls.label: Data integrations
controls.where: a project's Plan tab and the plan's approval card
controls.does: lists the databases, warehouses, cloud storage, ERPs and APIs the product reaches: how, whether it writes there, and what data it touches. A person declares one with the command rihmasto integration declare; IT binds each on a paved road and approves it on a road card before delivery

controls.label: Open Runners
controls.where: Settings
controls.does: opens the page that says which harness runs each role's cells and with what assurance

controls.label: Check the runners on this machine
controls.where: Runners, On this machine
controls.does: looks for Gnomon, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and a named command here, asks each its version, and says whether Docker can run the sandbox

controls.label: Choose a runner
controls.where: Runners
controls.does: chooses the builder's or the verifier's runner for the factory or one project: Gnomon at once, another harness on a card IT decides with its version pinned, optionally in a docker sandbox

controls.label: Approve a runner
controls.where: Runners, Choices (IT)
controls.does: approves or declines a runner waiting on IT; approved, it runs that role from then on and every round says it was checked after the run

controls.label: A project's cell runners
controls.where: Project settings
controls.does: shows what runs this project's builder and verifier and their assurance, with a link to change it in Settings > Runners

controls.label: Open Automations
controls.where: the sidebar; Home's card when the circuit breaker paused one; a project's Automations tab
controls.does: opens every automation across the factory, with scope filters and the history of runs

controls.label: New automation
controls.where: the Automations page header, or a project's Automations tab
controls.does: opens the builder: a trigger, an optional guard, an action, a scope and limits, with the summary the kernel writes before you save; it runs with your rights

controls.label: Start from a template
controls.where: the Automations page, or a project's Automations tab
controls.does: starts the builder from a common one: nightly re-gate, notify on release, re-scan a folder weekly, a cross-project dependency, ask after two failed gates, and the life-cycle ones: checks when a release reaches test, the probe check on promotion, a note when a concept is validated, a change proposal when the gate fails twice; a notice when a check fails, and re-reading the repository for alignment when it changes
synonyms: notify when a concept is validated

controls.label: Save the automation
controls.where: the automation builder
controls.does: saves the automation, signed with your name and persona; it acts with your rights from then on

controls.label: Run now
controls.where: each automation on the Automations page or a project's tab
controls.does: runs it once on the scheduler's next tick, passing over its trigger and guard; the runs per hour still hold

controls.label: Dry run
controls.where: each automation on the Automations page or a project's tab
controls.does: says what the next tick would do and records nothing

controls.label: Pause an automation
controls.where: each automation on the Automations page or a project's tab
controls.does: stops it until someone resumes it; anyone may pause one

controls.label: Resume an automation
controls.where: each paused automation on the Automations page or a project's tab
controls.does: runs it again after a pause or the circuit breaker; its owner or IT may

controls.label: Edit an automation
controls.where: each automation on the Automations page or a project's tab
controls.does: changes its parts; the person who changes it owns it from then on

controls.label: Remove an automation
controls.where: each automation on the Automations page or a project's tab
controls.does: removes it for good; its runs stay in the ledger

controls.label: Project tags
controls.where: a project's Automations tab
controls.does: tags the project, so an automation scoped to a tag reaches it

controls.label: Walkthroughs
controls.where: Home's header, and the top of the Ask Rihma panel
controls.does: lists the walkthroughs Rihma does with you in the chat, step by step: plug in an existing project, start from a new idea or from documents, set up a model, or get started with a tour. Each change waits for your Confirm, signed with your name

controls.label: Plug in an existing project
controls.where: Walkthroughs, in Ask Rihma
controls.does: asks for the folder or git address, scans it and shows in the chat what it found (files read, summarised, listed and skipped, the AI-tool setup, the languages, what looked secret), asks whether it is confidential, the intent and the posture, then adopts it when you press Adopt and waits for the result: the baseline, the kind of work and What's next

controls.label: Start from a new idea
controls.where: Walkthroughs, in Ask Rihma
controls.does: takes your idea in a sentence or two, then hands it to Shape it in chat, or makes a quick start (a title, one paragraph, the maturity) and waits for the intake's first questions

controls.label: Start from documents
controls.where: Walkthroughs, in Ask Rihma
controls.does: scans a spec or a folder of material in the chat, creates a new project from it when you press Create, and shows the intake's first questions

controls.label: Set up a model
controls.where: Walkthroughs, in Ask Rihma
controls.does: shows each role's model and readiness, offers a server on this machine, a hosted provider or a host on your own network, sets the role when you press Set, and runs Test in the chat

controls.label: Get started
controls.where: Walkthroughs, in Ask Rihma, and Home while there is no project
controls.does: a five-stop tour: Home, the Inbox, a project with What's next, Project settings, and Ask Rihma itself, each with Take me there and Next or Back

controls.label: Run a command
controls.where: a project's Console tab: the offered commands, or the command line
controls.does: runs one command in the project's workspace as a job, its output line by line; with Run through the shell for pipes and &&; signed and recorded as console_ran, never with what it printed

controls.label: Ask Gnomon in the workspace
controls.where: a project's Console tab, Ask Gnomon
controls.does: runs gnomon task in the workspace under its own surface and policy; gated changes are refused unless you tick Let Gnomon apply gated changes

controls.label: Stop the run
controls.where: a project's Console tab, beside the output
controls.does: stops the command and every process it started

controls.label: Open a terminal here
controls.where: a project's Console tab, under the workspace
controls.does: opens your operating system's terminal in the workspace, with the project's routing and Gnomon on PATH; only on the machine the cockpit runs on, from its own address

controls.label: Console settings
controls.where: a project's Console tab, for IT
controls.does: chooses which personas may run commands in the project's console, and states its test, build and lint commands

controls.label: Run a check now
controls.where: each check on a project's Health tab
controls.does: runs the check now and records its result: passed, failed or not measured with why

controls.label: Enable a check
controls.where: a project's Health tab, Enable a check
controls.does: enables a check on the project with its settings, a schedule and what a failure does (a signal, a change proposal)

controls.label: Disable a check
controls.where: each check on a project's Health tab
controls.does: stops the check; its results stay in the ledger

controls.label: Enable a check on several projects
controls.where: the Health page
controls.does: enables one check on the projects you tick, signed on each

controls.label: Insights dimension
controls.where: the filter row of Insights and of a project's Insights tab
controls.does: switches between health, compliance, governance, security, context drift, QA and usage

controls.label: Insights time window
controls.where: the filter row of Insights
controls.does: counts the records of the last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days or all of them; a tile compares with the window before

controls.label: Insights scope
controls.where: the filter row of Insights
controls.does: shows the whole factory or one project

controls.label: Export insights
controls.where: beside the filter row of Insights
controls.does: saves the figures as JSON, CSV or OpenTelemetry JSON (GenAI conventions for model runs) for your own observability tools; nothing is sent anywhere

controls.label: Pin to Home
controls.where: each tile on Insights
controls.does: adds that figure to your Home layout as an Insight widget

controls.label: Graph filters
controls.where: the filter panel of the Knowledge graph (a sheet on a phone)
controls.does: narrows the graph by node kind, relation, state (open, closed, superseded), time window and words, or to the nodes with an issue

controls.label: Graph or table
controls.where: the top of the Knowledge graph
controls.does: switches between the drawn graph and the table of nodes and relations; the table is the default on a phone, and your choice of default is saved

controls.label: Focus on a node
controls.where: the details of a node in the Knowledge graph
controls.does: shows only that node and what lies within one to four links of it

controls.label: Saved graph views
controls.where: beside the graph filters
controls.does: saves the filters as a named view for this project, opens a saved view, and resets to the default; saved for you

controls.label: Pin graph slice to Home
controls.where: beside the graph filters
controls.does: adds the current slice of the graph to your Home layout as a Knowledge graph widget

controls.label: Since you last looked
controls.where: Home, the first card
controls.does: says in one line what shipped, what waits on you and what failed since your last review, and opens the Review

controls.label: Mark all as seen
controls.where: the Review page and a project's Review tab, top right
controls.does: records that you looked at everything up to now, signed with your name; your next review starts there

controls.label: Reviewed
controls.where: a shipped task, release, output or gated commit on the Review page (key r)
controls.does: records a signed reviewed mark on that item, so its record shows a human looked; it approves nothing

controls.label: Morning digest
controls.where: the Review page, top right
controls.does: sends you the same review as a Teams, Slack or mail message at the time and days you set, with a link back to the Review; held back when nothing happened

controls.label: Paved roads
controls.where: Settings, the Paved roads card
controls.does: lists every road a product may deploy to (local process, docker, Azure Container Apps, Google Cloud Run) with its environments and rules, and says whether each is ready or exactly what is missing (an identity, a region, gcloud signed in on the deploying host)

controls.label: Configure a Google Cloud road
controls.where: Settings, the Paved roads card (IT)
controls.does: IT writes a Google Cloud Run road: the test and production projects, the region, the Artifact Registry repository, the identity Rihmasto deploys as and the one the product runs as, a service or a job run on a Cloud Scheduler schedule, the VPC egress and Secret Manager secrets by name; checked whole before it is written and recorded with who configured it
synonyms: run on a schedule in google cloud

controls.label: Choose the road
controls.where: a project's Releases tab, the Where it deploys card (IT)
controls.does: shows the road each environment of the plan lands on, ready or what is missing, and a scheduled job's last executions; IT chooses the project's road and, on Google Cloud, whether it runs as a service or a scheduled job with its cron, time zone and retries

controls.label: Google Drive connector
controls.where: Settings, the Integrations card
controls.does: a capability lists new files in a Google Drive folder, downloads one and uploads a result (a transcript) through the client app/gdrive.py, with its scopes stated and credentials named, never held: a token or key file by name for a local run, the runtime service account on Google Cloud

controls.label: Hand off to an agent
controls.where: a project's header
controls.does: gives a coding agent the project's brief (the goal or a change, the criteria, open questions, the plan, findings, failed gates and checks, conventions, how to run the tests and how to report back) with the way Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Cursor takes it: copy it, download it, or run it with the factory's chosen cell runner after a person accepts it; the hand-off is recorded
synonyms: give this to my coding agent

controls.label: Agent channel beside the view
controls.where: a project's header
controls.does: opens the project's agent channel as a panel beside whatever view is open, live
synonyms: watch the agents while i work

controls.label: Agents working on this
controls.where: a project's Overview
controls.does: shows the agents that worked on the project, their latest posts, the hand-offs given, the gate results and the proposals waiting on a person

controls.label: Post in the agent channel
controls.where: the Agent channel tab, below the messages
controls.does: posts your message, signed with your name and persona; @analyst or @verifier asks a Rihma agent, who answers from the records or through its model

controls.label: Pause the agent channel
controls.where: the Agent channel tab, above the messages
controls.does: makes the agents' posts wait and Rihma answer none until you resume it; resuming lets what waited through

controls.label: Confirm or reject an agent's proposed answer
controls.where: an agent's proposal in the Agent channel
controls.does: confirming answers the open question with the proposed text, signed with your name, through the Questions view's own route; rejecting keeps it open

controls.label: Trace of a message
controls.where: each message in the Agent channel
controls.does: shows what the message rests on: for a Rihma answer the rule and its sources or the Gnomon run (model, tokens, tool calls, duration); for an agent's post the commit, files and criteria; for a gate result its signals and objections

controls.label: Plan for a goal
controls.where: Ask Rihma, in a project
controls.does: answers a goal in your words (hook this to Google Drive, run it every night in our cloud, deploy to test, add sign-in, monitor it) with a plan from the project's records and what this Rihmasto has, gaps said plainly; each step is one click: draft a change, open the settings, a walkthrough, a command or a hand-off
synonyms: how do i get this to

controls.label: Live agent channels
controls.where: the Agent activity page
controls.does: lists every project's channel with who is talking, the last message, and the proposals waiting on a person

controls.label: Cancel the scan
controls.where: New project's scan step, while a long scan runs
controls.does: stops the scan of a large folder; the step shows the files looked at, the time and the folder while it runs

controls.label: Allow a folder from the scan
controls.where: New project's scan step, when a folder is outside the allowed ones
controls.does: allows the folder's top folder (a single operator, after saying yes) so the scan runs at once; under enforced access it says to ask IT

controls.label: Adopt it again as a new project
controls.where: New project's scan step, when the folder or repository is already adopted
controls.does: makes a second project on purpose; Open <project> takes you to the one already adopted

controls.label: The last commit or the working copy
controls.where: New project's scan step, when a git repository has uncommitted work
controls.does: adopts the last commit (the default; uncommitted changes and untracked files are left out) or the working copy as it is now as a snapshot; the map shows exactly what is taken

controls.label: Adopt each or the folder as one
controls.where: New project's scan step, when a folder holds several git repositories
controls.does: adopts each chosen repository as its own project, or the whole folder as one snapshot; copies (a _snapshot, -copy, -prep folder) are read once

controls.label: Use my local model for these roles
controls.where: New project's scan step, for a confidential adoption
controls.does: points the roles routed to a hosted model at the local or private model the routing already has, signed and recorded in Models setup; adopting itself calls no model

controls.label: Track and evaluate this work
controls.where: New project's scan step, for a folder of documents only
controls.does: adopts the documents as a body of work in a monitoring state (an experiment, a report), with no build questions; Build something from these documents starts a new project from them instead

controls.label: How is it used today
controls.where: New project's scan step, An existing project
controls.does: sets the adopted project's maturity: an experiment, a prototype, in use by a few or in production, inferred from its files until you say

controls.label: Folders the cockpit may read
controls.where: Settings
controls.does: lists the home folder, the operator's RIHMASTO_SOURCE_ROOTS and the folders allowed here; IT (or a single operator, after saying yes) allows one without a restart; system folders and folders of keys never

controls.label: Kind: not chosen yet
controls.where: the project header
controls.does: says no kind of work is chosen while Which kind of work is this? is open; answer it or choose one in Project settings

controls.label: Adopted state
controls.where: an adopted project's header and Overview
controls.does: shows what the adopted project is doing (monitoring, maintaining, improving), what was taken, its baseline and the command that made it, instead of the seven stages

controls.label: Set up the watch
controls.where: an adopted project's Overview, Watching
controls.does: watches it through the automations: new commits as a summary in Review and the timeline, the activity by area weekly, failed checks to a channel

controls.label: Run a stated command as the baseline
controls.where: an adopted project's Overview, Stated test commands
controls.does: runs a test command the project's instructions state, which the kernel does not run on its own, after your yes (it runs the project's code), and records which command produced the baseline

controls.label: Areas
controls.where: an adopted project's Overview
controls.does: shows what each top-level folder holds (files, asset kinds such as models, textures, audio and scenes) and what moved over 30 days, with the design and lore documents
synonyms: how are the assets coming along

controls.label: Guide me step by step
controls.where: Ask Rihma, in an answer about a journey, and the Overview's Next step card
controls.does: opens the guided panel at the top of Ask Rihma: the journey's steps measured from the records, the current one highlighted with Do it, I did it, Skip and Stop; it stays with you across views and after a reload, and shows each step's result as it completes

controls.label: Do it
controls.where: the guided panel in Ask Rihma
controls.does: does the current step through its own route, signed with your name (Run the assessment, Read the repository, Set up the watch), starts the walkthrough that does it (choose the folder, scan, adopt), or opens the place where you do it with the control highlighted

controls.label: I did it
controls.where: the guided panel in Ask Rihma
controls.does: records your word that a step no record can show is done (the IDE section pasted, a model answered), signed with your name; a step the records show is measured, not marked

controls.label: Skip
controls.where: the guided panel in Ask Rihma
controls.does: skips the current step for this guide, signed with your name, and offers the next one

controls.label: Stop guiding
controls.where: the guided panel in Ask Rihma
controls.does: ends the guide; what was done stays, and Guide me step by step starts again where the records say you are

controls.label: Next step
controls.where: a project's Overview
controls.does: says where the project is on its journey (fed in, from an idea, from documents), the next step and why, with its button and its command, and Guide me step by step

controls.label: Three ways in
controls.where: Projects and Home while there is no project
controls.does: offers the three journeys to start with, feed in an existing project, start from a new idea or start from documents, each one guided step by step

controls.label: Browse… (choose a folder or a file)
controls.where: beside every field that takes a folder or a file on the cockpit's machine: New project (An existing project, and a folder as the need), Add material, Shape it in chat's attach, Settings > Folders the cockpit may read, an automation's rescan folder, a Google Cloud road's workload identity file, and a walkthrough's folder step
controls.does: opens this computer's own folder dialog when you sit at the cockpit's machine (a single operator's cockpit on 127.0.0.1); from another computer, a phone or under enforced access it opens the folder browser in the page instead. Choosing a project's folder goes straight to the scan

controls.label: Browse here (the folder browser)
controls.where: beside every Browse… button
controls.does: browses the cockpit's folders in the page, from anywhere: recent folders, the allowed roots, the home folder and the drives; each folder says whether it is a git repository, already a project here, and whether the cockpit may read it (Allow it offers to allow one); filter as you type, use the arrow keys, Enter and Backspace, then Choose this folder. Hidden and tool folders (dot folders, node_modules, .venv) are folded; a link out of the allowed folders is never followed; system folders and folders of keys are never read

controls.label: Context pack of an agent
controls.where: the project's Context view
controls.does: opens what one Rihma agent is given right now (the intake panel, the spec, the holdout author, the builder's envelope, the verifier, Ask Rihma, goal help, an agent channel answer, the hand-off brief or the MCP tools): each part with its source, size and estimated tokens, what was compressed and what was left out and why
synonyms: what is sent to the model

controls.label: Compression findings
controls.where: the project's Context view
controls.does: lists what the compression audit found in this project's packs: over budget, said twice, a changing part before a stable one, oversized tool answers, conventions sent where they are not needed, each with a proposed compression

controls.label: Context health
controls.where: the Data and context page
controls.does: shows, per agent role, the average and largest context pack, how many are over budget and how much of each call a prompt cache can reuse, with what was compressed before and after

controls.label: Propose a clean-up
controls.where: the Data and context page
controls.does: proposes, signed with your name, removing what can go safely (job logs and unreferenced snapshots older than 30 days); ledgers, records and the holdout custody are never cleaned

controls.label: Apply a clean-up
controls.where: the Data and context page
controls.does: carries out a clean-up proposal as IT or operations, each item checked unchanged first, and records what was removed

controls.label: Destinations map
controls.where: a project's Destinations tab
controls.does: shows every place the capability goes, grouped as deployed, data, channels and published, each with its environment, state, last delivery and health

controls.label: Where this goes
controls.where: a project's Overview
controls.does: says in one line where the capability runs, the data it reaches, the channels it is used through and where it is published, with the way to Destinations

controls.label: Deliver to test
controls.where: a test environment's card on the Destinations tab
controls.does: starts the delivery of main's revision by the project's plan, signed with your name: built, deployed to the test environment and smoke-checked

controls.label: Promote to production
controls.where: the production card on the Destinations tab
controls.does: goes on with the delivery toward production, signed with your name; it stops at IT's deploy gate, which decides

controls.label: Publish to a registry
controls.where: a registry's card on the Destinations tab, or the MCP face's card
controls.does: pushes the release's container image to the registry IT named (test first; production through IT's deploy gate), or writes the MCP registry entry for you to submit; a registry that is not ready says exactly what is missing

controls.label: Check the destinations now
controls.where: the Destinations tab, top right
controls.does: probes every environment where it runs and reads every destination again; one that became failing opens an incident, posts in the agent channel and is recorded for the Review and the automations

controls.label: Investigate a failing destination
controls.where: a failing card on the Destinations tab
controls.does: opens the incident in the Inbox, where operations, IT or a developer decides it

controls.label: Set up this project
controls.where: a project's Overview, at the top until everything that applies is set up
controls.does: lists every feature of Rihmasto that applies to the project (checks and Health, automations, alignment, Insights and Review, AI tools and the agent channel, posture, outputs) with its state: set up, offered, or not applicable and why

controls.label: One click in the set-up checklist
controls.where: each offered item of Set up this project
controls.does: does that item, signed with your name (enables a check, sets up the suggested automation, reads the repository for alignment) or opens the place where you choose

controls.label: Suggested automations
controls.where: a project's Automations tab, and the Automations page for a project you pick
controls.does: scans the project's shape and state (its repository, tests, releases, checks, whether it is confidential, its profile) and suggests automations with a one-line reason each

controls.label: Set up a suggested automation
controls.where: a suggestion in Suggested automations
controls.does: sets the suggested automation up in your name, signed, with one click

controls.label: Dismiss a suggested automation
controls.where: a suggestion in Suggested automations
controls.does: stops offering that suggestion on this project; remembered and recorded

controls.label: Describe it
controls.where: the Automations page and a project's Automations tab
controls.does: turns your words (every night run the tests and tell me on Teams if they fail) into a draft automation with its summary and a dry run, which you then set up or open in the builder

controls.label: Archive this project
controls.where: Project settings, at the bottom
controls.does: hides the project from every list and makes it read-only, restorable from Projects, Archived; signed and recorded

controls.label: Archived projects
controls.where: the Projects page, below the projects
controls.does: lists the archived projects and the duplicates (projects that share a title) with the copies to archive

controls.label: Restore a project
controls.where: Projects, Archived
controls.does: brings an archived project back into the lists, writable again; recorded

controls.label: Remove a project
controls.where: Projects, Archived, beside an archived project
controls.does: removes an archived project for good after you type its id: it cannot be undone, and its records are kept first as an export file

controls.label: Map to the hub's project
controls.where: a project's Agent sessions view
controls.does: maps the project to the agent observability hub's project for its repository (suggested by its catalog annotation, git remote or folder name); a developer or IT confirms, signed and recorded

controls.label: Record what the hub shows
controls.where: a project's Agent sessions view
controls.does: records the figures the hub shows (sessions by harness, unrecovered failures, heavily reworked files, contract read first, the chain's verdict) in the project's ledger; counts and ids only

controls.label: Agent observability hub address
controls.where: Settings, once Agent observability is on for a project or the factory
controls.does: IT sets the hub's address (loopback or private at once, a hosted one only with explicit consent over https) and names the token's environment variable

controls.label: Turn on Agent sessions
controls.where: the AI tools card of an adopted or attached project worked on in IDEs
controls.does: turns Agent observability on for this project, signed and recorded

controls.label: Agent observability hub hooks
controls.where: the AI tools card of an adopted or attached project
controls.does: says whether the repository carries the agent observability hub's hooks, by file names only, and offers the module

controls.label: People and access
controls.where: Settings, People and access
controls.does: says in plain words who works here: solo (one person acting in every persona, each decision naming the persona it used), a team (people and identity-provider groups deciding as the personas they hold), or IT's access file; and holds every setting below

controls.label: Solo or team mode
controls.where: Settings, People and access, and the first visit's Just me or A team
controls.does: turns team mode on (personas become people and groups; you become the first user and every record stays) or goes back to just you

controls.label: Your name in solo mode
controls.where: Settings, People and access
controls.does: sets the one person's name that signs every decision in solo mode
synonyms: change my name in solo mode

controls.label: Add a user
controls.where: Settings, People and access, People
controls.does: adds a person to the team with the personas they hold, on every project or one

controls.label: Invite link
controls.where: Settings, People and access, beside each person
controls.does: makes a one-use sign-in link for a person (a week for an invite), shown once; only its hash is kept and no password ever is

controls.label: Deactivate a user
controls.where: Settings, People and access, beside each person
controls.does: stops a person's sessions and links at their next request; activate brings them back

controls.label: Map a group to a persona
controls.where: Settings, People and access, Groups from your identity provider
controls.does: lets everyone in an identity provider's group (Entra ID object id or app role, AWS, Google, any OIDC) decide as a persona, on every project or one

controls.label: A project's own roles
controls.where: Settings, People and access
controls.does: on one project, a person holds exactly the personas named there, whatever they hold elsewhere

controls.label: Pages per persona
controls.where: Settings, People and access
controls.does: keeps pages such as Insights or Automations from a persona in team mode (who sees which projects follows the personas' projects)
synonyms: hide a page from a persona

controls.label: Identity provider
controls.where: Settings, People and access
controls.does: names team mode's identity provider (Entra ID, AWS ALB, Google IAP or any OIDC proxy): issuer, address, audience and groups claim, checked as IT's access file is

controls.label: Fetch the provider's keys
controls.where: Settings, People and access, Identity provider
controls.does: fetches the provider's public signing keys once from its JWKS address (or takes them pasted); public keys only, and every change is recorded

controls.label: Test with a token
controls.where: Settings, People and access, Identity provider
controls.does: shows who a token from the provider would sign in as: identity, name, groups and personas, or why it is refused; it records nothing

controls.label: Give a persona to an agent
controls.where: Settings, People and access, Agents acting as a persona
controls.does: gives a persona you hold to an agent on one project by delegation: the kinds of card it may decide, until a date at most a week away; it never decides anything else, and revoking it on the Track view stops it at once
synonyms: delegate a persona to an agent

controls.label: Agents acting as a persona
controls.where: Settings, People and access
controls.does: lists every persona given to an agent, as operations: delegated to ops-agent until a date

controls.label: Viewing as: everything
controls.where: the person menu (Everything), and the Inbox's Cards you decide as
controls.does: shows every card you may decide in any persona you hold; each decision is signed with the persona it needs and the record names it. Pick a persona to look through its lens instead

controls.label: Run a Gnomon audit
controls.where: a project's Health tab, Audits & evals
controls.does: runs one of Gnomon's audits, benchmarks or evals on the project's repository as a job whose log streams on the Jobs page, and records its result: passed, failed or not measured with why, its scores and findings (eval ids: security, security_test, compliance, dataflow, metrics, audit_verify, check, eval, chaos, doctor, claim_check, context_cost, degradation)

controls.label: Make a finding a change
controls.where: each finding under Audits & evals on a project's Health tab
controls.does: files the audit's finding, with its evidence, as a change proposal in the Inbox, signed with your name
synonyms: turn the finding into a change

controls.label: Audit history
controls.where: each audit under Audits & evals on a project's Health tab
controls.does: shows the audit's last runs: verdicts, scores and how many issues were new or resolved

controls.label: Audits across projects
controls.where: the Health page, Audits & evals
controls.does: lists every project's latest Gnomon audit results and new issues, and what Gnomon this machine has

controls.label: Compare models on Rihma's evals
controls.where: Models setup, On our evals
controls.does: runs Rihma's own eval sets per role (intake questions, spec testability, Ask Rihma answers, goal plans) against the configured model and its alternatives, as a job, and shows each model's score per set

controls.label: Incidents
controls.where: the sidebar, What's next, Home and Review
controls.does: opens the incidents: open, investigating, fixed and learned

controls.label: Something's wrong here
controls.where: the foot of every view, and the panel shown in place of an error
controls.does: reports what you see as an incident with the view's context, signed with your name

controls.label: This is unclear / this is wrong
controls.where: the foot of every view and each Ask Rihma answer
controls.does: records your feedback on the words shown; repeated feedback becomes a wording, assistant rule or prompt change a person approves

controls.label: Investigate with Rihma
controls.where: each incident, and the panel shown in place of an error
controls.does: a Rihma agent reads the incident's context and records, posts its diagnosis with a trace in the incident's channel thread, classifies it and proposes the next step

controls.label: A remedy
controls.where: each incident, and the panel shown in place of an error
controls.does: takes a remedy Rihmasto offers: a learned one first, then the built-in ones (start it on its road, Models setup, run it again, try again)

controls.label: This fixed it
controls.where: each incident
controls.does: resolves the incident with what fixed it, which Rihmasto proposes as a remedy for next time

controls.label: Approve remedy
controls.where: What Rihmasto learned, on the Incidents page
controls.does: approves a learned remedy once, signed: offered first from now on, applied on its own only when it is safe

controls.label: Retire remedy
controls.where: What Rihmasto learned, on the Incidents page
controls.does: stops offering a learned remedy

controls.label: Prepare the fix
controls.where: an investigated incident
controls.does: takes the proposed fix (a reproducing test and the change) through the gate on a branch of its own: fail-first, the suite, the verifier

controls.label: Approve and open the pull request
controls.where: a fix the gate passed
controls.does: on your approval pushes the fix's branch and opens its pull request with gh (or gives the exact commands); never a default branch, never merged by Rihmasto

controls.label: Approve wording change
controls.where: Feedback, on the Incidents page
controls.does: approves or rejects a wording, assistant rule or prompt change proposed from repeated feedback; approved changes apply from a data file
